tagline: Along the Deschutes canyon on an old railroad grade.
intro: The byway keeps to the east bank of the Lower Deschutes for 32 miles, with close views of the rapids in steep canyon country, between Locked Gate Day Use Area at the south end and the campground at Macks Canyon at the north. Twelve miles are paved, from Maupin to Highway 216 near Sherars Falls. The rest is good gravel, fit for passenger cars.
Much of the way is an old railbed, one of two whose owners once raced each other to finish. The river keeps the road company the whole way.

moments.title: Sherars Falls
moments.text: At the last falls on the Deschutes, about fifteen feet of class 6 water, tribal fishermen still work salmon and steelhead with dip nets from the boulders and their own platforms.

moments.title: Maupin
moments.text: A ferry crossing that became a river town of about 400, where US 197 crosses the Deschutes at one of the few places it can be crossed north of Madras.

moments.title: Section Foreman's House
moments.text: Just south of Maupin the railroad section foreman's house still stands beside the road, restored and opened in season with displays and river news.

sources.label: BLM, Lower Deschutes River Back Country Byway
